statement: Game theory: Expected payoff and die choice. (a) We play a game where you roll a fair die to get number $X$, and I roll a fair die to get number $Y$. Your payoff is $\max(X-Y, 0)$. Give an 80\% confidence interval for how much you would pay to play this game. (b) Calculate the exact expected payoff. (c) You now have the option to switch your fair die to one with faces showing three 1s and three 6s. Should you switch? (d) Instead, you have the option to switch my fair die to one with three 1s and three 6s. Should you make this switch?

title: Bayesian Coin Selection After Observing Heads
statement: Bayesian inference: Biased coins and betting. You have two coins. The first coin has a 2/3 probability of heads, and the second has a 1/3 probability of heads. We randomly pick one coin and flip it 3 times, resulting in 3 heads. (a) What is the probability that the next flip with this same coin will be a head? (b) Counterparty A offers you a bet: if the next flip is a head, you win \$1; otherwise, you lose \$1. Would you take this bet? If offered multiple times, would you take it? (c) Counterparty B offers a different bet: if it's a head, you lose \$1; if it's a tail, you win \$1.5. Would you take it? (d) If you could take bet B at most once and bet A up to one hundred times, how would you choose?

title: St. Petersburg Paradox with Uniform Reciprocal
statement: St. Petersburg Paradox variant. You play a game where a random number $X$ is drawn from a uniform distribution on $(0,1)$, and you are paid $1/X$. (a) How much would you be willing to pay to play this game? (b) How do you deal with the problem of infinite expectation?

title: Probability: Expected cards to draw for first Ace
statement: Probability: Expected cards to draw for first Ace. What is the expected number of cards you need to draw from a standard 52-card deck to see the first Ace?

title: Linear algebra: Sudoku matrix eigenvalue
statement: Linear algebra: Sudoku matrix eigenvalue. For a valid, completed 9x9 Sudoku matrix, find one eigenvalue and its corresponding eigenvector.

title: Quant Developer Phone Screen Topics
statement: Interview topics: CTC Quant Developer Phone Screen. The interview covered variations of ball weighing problems, dynamic programming for betting games, Bayesian probability problems, variations of the coin change problem, and elementary math Olympiad-style questions.

title: Quant Developer Onsite Interview Topics
statement: Interview topics: CTC Quant Developer Onsite. The onsite interviews included a system design round, a C++ code refactoring exercise using specific design patterns, pointers, and OOP concepts, a round on Python fundamentals, pandas, and algorithms, and a round of pure brain teasers.

title: Probability: Expected number of adjacent cat-dog pairs
statement: Probability: Expected number of adjacent cat-dog pairs. You arrange 9 cats and 8 dogs in a row of 17 places. What is the expected number of pairs where a dog is sitting next to a cat?

title: Balls of Three Colors Combination Count
statement: Combinatorics: Balls of three colors. A big bag contains an infinite number of balls of three different colors. (a) If you randomly pick 3 balls from the bag, what is the number of possible combinations of colors? (b) What if you pick $n$ balls? (Solve using stars and bars or integer programming).

title: Cumulative Dice Sum Threshold Distribution
statement: Probability: Distribution before exceeding a threshold. You repeatedly roll a fair six-sided die until the cumulative sum of the rolls exceeds 63. What is the distribution of the last cumulative sum that was not over 63 (i.e., the value right before the final roll)? The possible values are 58, 59, 60, 61, 62, 63.

title: Random Forest and Bagging Variance Reduction
statement: Machine learning: Random Forest and Bagging. (a) What is a Random Forest? How does it differ from a single Decision Tree? (b) What is Bagging? (c) Why does incorporating random feature selection at each split help reduce the variance of the model?

title: Linear Regression Assumptions and Violations
statement: Statistics: Assumptions and issues in Linear Regression. (a) What are the assumptions of the classic Linear Regression model? (b) Does multicollinearity bias the coefficient estimates? (c) How does heteroskedasticity affect the coefficient estimates? (d) What are the implications if the residuals follow a t-distribution instead of a normal distribution?

title: Linear Interpolation from Sorted Pairs
statement: Coding: Linear interpolation. Given a sorted array of pairs `A = [[x_1, y_1], [x_2, y_2], ...]` and a target value `x`, return the linearly interpolated value of `y` at `x`. For example, given `A = [[0, 1], [2, 4], [5, 7], [8, 6]]`, `f(1)` should return `2.5`, and `f(7)` should return `6.33`. Optimize the time complexity from O(n) to O(log n).

title: Coding: Merge sorted array
statement: Coding: Merge sorted array. Given two sorted arrays `A` and `B`, merge `B` into `A` as one sorted array. Assume `A` has enough space at the end to hold `B`. This is LeetCode problem 88.

title: Pandas Grouped Mean and Weighted Mean
statement: Pandas: Data manipulation. Using the pandas library, perform the following operations: (a) Calculate the mean of a certain feature, grouped by a 'name' column. (b) Calculate the weighted mean of a certain feature, grouped by a 'name' column, given a weights column.

title: Onsite Data Analysis Project Case Study
statement: Case study: Onsite data analysis project. You are given a dataset and asked to perform a full data analysis project on-site. This includes data cleaning, exploratory analysis, modeling, and presenting your findings.

title: OLS Regression of X on Y vs Y on X
statement: Statistics: OLS regression of X on Y vs. Y on X. Consider two OLS regressions: $Y \sim X$ and $X \sim Y$. (a) How are the estimated slope coefficients ($\beta_{Y|X}$ and $\beta_{X|Y}$) and the coefficients of determination ($R^2$) related? (b) Which regression line is steeper? Provide a proof. (c) This asymmetry can be a problem. How can Principal Component Analysis (PCA) be used to find a symmetric line of best fit?

title: House Price Feature Sign and Collinearity
statement: Open-ended: House price prediction model. You want to estimate house prices using apartment size and the number of bathrooms as features. (a) What sign do you expect for the coefficients of these variables in a linear regression? (b) If two variables in a linear regression model are highly correlated, what happens to your model? (c) How can you solve this problem? (e.g., using PCA).

title: Coding: String multiplication
statement: Coding: String multiplication. Implement a function to multiply two non-negative integers represented as strings. You should also write your own test cases. This is LeetCode problem 43.

title: Principal Components of Stock Covariance Matrix
statement: Time series: Principal Components of covariance matrix. In the context of time series analysis of multiple stocks, what is the financial or economic interpretation of the principal components of the stock return covariance matrix?

title: Spectral Decomposition for Multivariate Normal
statement: Statistics: Simulating multivariate normal via spectral decomposition. How can you sample $N$ random variables from a multivariate normal distribution with a given covariance matrix $\Sigma$ without using Cholesky decomposition? (Hint: use spectral decomposition).

title: Confidence Interval with Zero Successes
statement: Statistics: Confidence interval for binomial p with zero successes. A coin is tossed $N$ times, and 0 heads are observed. Derive a confidence interval for the probability of heads, $p$. Compare frequentist and Bayesian approaches.

title: Quantitative finance: Portfolio optimization
statement: Quantitative finance: Portfolio optimization. Solve a simple, textbook-level portfolio optimization problem (e.g., finding the minimum variance portfolio for two assets).

title: Mathematical proof
statement: Mathematical proof. Prove that $\pi$ is not an integer.

title: Python Hashable Objects and Custom Classes
statement: Python: Hashable objects and custom classes. (a) What types of objects can be stored in a Python `set`? (b) If you define a custom class, can an instance of this class be stored in a `set`? If so, what is required?

title: Python: '\_\_new\_\_' vs
statement: Python: `\_\_new\_\_` vs. `\_\_init\_\_`. What is the difference between the `\_\_new\_\_` and `\_\_init\_\_` methods in Python classes?

title: Pirate Hat Puzzle Cooperative Strategy
statement: Brain teaser: The hat puzzle. There are 10 pirates. Each is randomly assigned a red or blue hat. Each pirate can see the hats of all other pirates but not their own. They must all simultaneously guess the color of their own hat. If everyone guesses correctly, they are all released. If even one person guesses incorrectly, they are all executed. They can confer on a strategy beforehand. What strategy maximizes their probability of survival, and what is that probability?

title: Estimation with Equicorrelated Normal Samples
statement: Statistics: Estimation with equicorrelated normal samples. You have $n$ samples from a normal distribution $N(\mu, 1)$, but they are not i.i.d. The correlation matrix has off-diagonal elements that are all equal to a constant $r$. (a) How would you estimate $\mu$? (b) What is the test statistic for a hypothesis test on $\mu$? (c) What is the valid range of values for $r$?

title: Airbnb Price Rationality Case Study
statement: Case study: Airbnb price rationality. (a) How would you determine if an Airbnb host's listed price is reasonable? What features would you need? (b) A problem is that some listings have very few ratings. How would you incorporate or handle the ratings feature? (c) Pricing is relative to the neighborhood. How would you incorporate location and prices of nearby comparable listings?

title: Statistics: Confidence intervals for logistic regression parameters
statement: Statistics: Confidence intervals for logistic regression parameters. If you fit a logistic regression model, how do you calculate the confidence intervals for the model's parameters?

title: Linear Recurrence via Matrix Exponentiation
statement: Coding: Efficiently computing a linear recurrence. Consider the recurrence relation $f(n) = 2f(n-1) + f(n-2)$. (a) Write a recursive function to compute $f(n)$. Analyze its time complexity. (b) Optimize the function using memoization (dynamic programming). What is the time and space complexity? (c) Further optimize to use constant space. (d) Discuss the complexity implications if $n$ is very large, considering the cost of arithmetic operations on large numbers.

title: OLS Model Comparison Bias-Variance Tradeoff
statement: Statistics: OLS model comparison. Consider two models: $M_1: y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2 + \epsilon$ and $M_2: y = \gamma_0 + \gamma_1 x_1 + \eta$. If you are only interested in the effect of $x_1$, which model is better? Compare the bias and variance of the estimators for the coefficient of $x_1$ in both models. Compare their Mean Squared Error (MSE). Can you describe a scenario where $M_2$ would be preferred over $M_1$?

title: Effect of Demeaning Variables in OLS
statement: Statistics: Effect of demeaning variables in OLS. In Ordinary Least Squares regression, does demeaning the variables (subtracting the mean from each observation) before running the regression change the estimated slope coefficients? Does it change the intercept? Explain.

title: Probability: Expectation of a ratio of IID variables
statement: Probability: Expectation of a ratio of IID variables. For two positive i.i.d. random variables $X$ and $Y$, prove that $E[X/Y] \ge 1$.

title: Statistics: OLS assumptions
statement: Statistics: OLS assumptions. Discuss the assumptions of the Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) model and their geometric meaning.

title: Coding: Find next palindrome
statement: Coding: Find next palindrome. Given an integer, find the smallest palindrome that is strictly larger than the given number. This is a simplified version of LeetCode problem 564.

title: Sorting Algorithm Design and Complexity
statement: Algorithm concept: Sorting. You are presented with a problem related to sorting, but you are not required to write code. You must describe an efficient algorithm and justify its correctness and complexity.

title: Probability on a graph
statement: Probability on a graph. Solve a simple probability problem set on a graph structure (e.g., random walks, finding probabilities of reaching certain nodes).

title: Sharpe Ratio Aggregation and Annualization
statement: Quantitative finance: Sharpe Ratio concepts. (a) What is the range of the combined Sharpe ratio of ten different models? (b) How do you convert a daily Sharpe ratio to an annual Sharpe ratio? (c) Why might the actual annualized performance differ from the theoretical annualized Sharpe ratio?

title: Markov Decision Process for Stock Trading
statement: Dynamic programming: Markov decision process for stocks. A stock trading scenario involves rewards and penalties. Formulate this as a dynamic programming problem to maximize the expected return. This can be modeled as a Markov decision process. Describe the states, actions, and transition probabilities.

title: Maximizing Taxi Driver Revenue Strategy
statement: Case study: Maximizing a taxi driver's revenue. As a taxi driver in New York City, how would you strategize to maximize your profit? Discuss your objective function, what factors to consider, and what data you would use.

title: Coding: Diophantine equation
statement: Coding: Diophantine equation. Write a program to find the number of positive integer solutions $(x,y)$ to the equation $\frac{1}{N!} = \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y}$ for a given integer $N$.

title: Case study: Predicting Citi Bike distribution
statement: Case study: Predicting Citi Bike distribution. How would you build a model to predict the distribution of Citi Bikes throughout New York City at a future time?

title: Bayesian Hierarchical Coin Toss Correlation
statement: Bayesian hierarchical model: Correlation of counts. A coin's probability of heads, $p$, is itself a random variable drawn from some distribution. Let $N_{100}$ be the number of heads in 100 tosses and $N_{10}$ be the number of heads in the first 10 of those tosses. What is the correlation between $N_{100}$ and $N_{10}$?

title: Evaluating Probabilistic Weather Forecasters
statement: Case study: Evaluating weather forecasters. You have access to forecasts from several experts. Each day, each expert provides a probability $p$ that it will rain. How do you evaluate these forecasts over time to determine who is the "best" forecaster?

title: Case study: Airbnb pricing model
statement: Case study: Airbnb pricing model. Design a model for pricing an Airbnb rental. Discuss features, model selection, and validation. (This is a repeat of problem 142).

title: General Prediction Modeling Process
statement: Case study: General prediction model. You are given a prediction task. Explain your modeling process, including the choice of model, feature engineering, and how you would prevent overfitting and perform feature selection.

title: Coding: Pandas data processing
statement: Coding: Pandas data processing. Solve a data processing task using the pandas library that involves algorithmic thinking beyond simple manipulations.

title: CS fundamentals: TreeMap vs
statement: CS fundamentals: TreeMap vs. HashMap. Compare and contrast TreeMap and HashMap (or equivalent ordered and unordered dictionary structures) in terms of implementation, performance, and use cases.

title: Hash Table Implementation and Collision Resolution
statement: CS fundamentals: Hash table implementation. Explain how a hash table is implemented. Discuss hash functions, collision resolution strategies (e.g., chaining, open addressing), and performance characteristics.

title: CS fundamentals: Thread vs
statement: CS fundamentals: Thread vs. process. (a) What is the difference between a thread and a process? (b) How can two processes communicate and exchange data with each other (Inter-Process Communication)?

title: CS fundamentals: Design patterns
statement: CS fundamentals: Design patterns. Give an example of a software design pattern and explain its purpose and structure.

title: Portfolio theory: Fund allocation
statement: Portfolio theory: Fund allocation. How would you approach the problem of allocating capital among various investment opportunities or strategies?

title: Portfolio theory: Reducing volatility
statement: Portfolio theory: Reducing volatility. If you have a large number of stocks, what methods can be used to construct a portfolio that reduces overall volatility?

title: CS fundamentals: Sorting algorithms
statement: CS fundamentals: Sorting algorithms. Name a sorting algorithm and state its time complexity (best, average, worst case).

title: Algorithm: Find common elements in two arrays
statement: Algorithm: Find common elements in two arrays. Describe an efficient algorithm to find the common elements between two arrays.

title: OLS: Slopes of x~y vs
statement: OLS: Slopes of x~y vs. y~x. What is the relationship between the slope coefficients from a regression of Y on X and a regression of X on Y? (This is a repeat of problem 130).

title: Suppressor Variables in Multiple Regression
statement: OLS: Suppressor variables. In a multiple regression $y \sim x_1 + x_2$, the t-statistics for both $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$ are significant. However, in a simple regression $y \sim x_1$, the t-statistic for $\beta_1$ is not significant. What is a possible reason for this? Provide an example.

title: Probability: Expected tosses for consecutive heads
statement: Probability: Expected tosses for consecutive heads. What is the expected number of tosses of a fair coin required to get three consecutive heads?

title: Convergence in Probability vs Almost Sure
statement: Probability theory: Modes of convergence. (a) What is the definition of convergence in probability? (b) What is the definition of almost sure convergence? (c) Give a classic counterexample of a sequence of random variables that converges in probability but does not converge almost surely.

title: Citi Bike Availability Forecasting
statement: Case study: Citi Bike prediction. How would you forecast the number of Citi Bikes available at a specific location in a city at a future time? Discuss your approach, including feature engineering, standardization, feature selection, and model creation. (This is a repeat of problem 157).

title: Coding: Wildcard matching
statement: Coding: Wildcard matching. Given an input string `s` and a pattern `p`, implement wildcard pattern matching with support for '?' and '*'. This is LeetCode problem 44.

title: Optimal Worker-Task Assignment Problem
statement: Algorithm: The assignment problem. There are $2n$ workers and two types of tasks, Task 1 and Task 2. There are $n$ instances of each task. For each worker $i$, you are given the time they take to complete Task 1 ($w_{i1}$) and Task 2 ($w_{i2}$). Assign each worker to one task such that all $2n$ tasks are completed and the total time taken is minimized.

title: Algorithm: Sorting large arrays
statement: Algorithm: Sorting large arrays. What is the most efficient algorithm to sort a very large array, under the constraint that you can only compare two elements at a time?

title: Game theory: Lottery expectation
statement: Game theory: Lottery expectation. How do you decide which lottery ticket to buy? Frame this as a problem of maximizing expected return.

title: Probability: Variance and expectation inequality
statement: Probability: Variance and expectation inequality. Which is larger, $E[X^2]$ or $(E[X])^2$? Under what conditions are they equal?

title: Probability: Bounds on P(B)
statement: Probability: Bounds on P(B). Given the probabilities $P(A)$ and $P(A \cap B)$, what is the possible range of values for $P(B)$?

title: Finance: FX contract volatility
statement: Finance: FX contract volatility. Discuss the concept of volatility in the context of foreign exchange (FX) contracts.

title: Uber vs Taxi Driver Strategy Comparison
statement: Open-ended: Uber vs. taxi driver strategy. Suppose you are a taxi driver aiming to maximize your profit. Now, suppose you are an Uber driver instead. Is there any difference in your optimal strategy? (This is a follow-up to problem 154).

title: Linear Interpolation with Edge Cases
statement: Data analysis: Linear interpolation. Given a set of $(x_i, y_i)$ pairs, where $x_i$ is sorted, implement a function for linear interpolation. Handle edge cases like repeated $x_i$ values. (This is a repeat of problem 126).

title: Maximizing R-Squared with Variable Selection
statement: Data analysis: Maximizing R-squared. Given a dataset with 5 independent variables (X) and one dependent variable (Y), find (a) the single X variable and (b) the pair of X variables that produce the highest in-sample $R^2$ in a linear regression.

title: Best Subset Selection for R-Squared
statement: Feature selection: Best subset for R-squared. As a follow-up to the previous problem, describe a method to select a subset of the 5 independent variables to perform a linear regression that achieves an approximately maximal $R^2$. An exact solution is not required.

title: LRU Cache Data Structure Design
statement: Coding: LRU Cache. Design and implement a data structure for a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache. It should support the `get` and `put` operations in O(1) average time complexity. This is LeetCode problem 146.

title: Median from a Data Stream
statement: Coding: Median from Data Stream. Design a data structure that supports the following two operations: `addNum(num)` which adds an integer from a data stream to the data structure, and `findMedian()` which returns the median of all elements so far. This is LeetCode problem 295.

title: Bayesian Methods and Overfitting Prevention
statement: Machine Learning: General Discussion. Discuss general machine learning concepts, including: (a) How Bayesian methods can be applied in machine learning. (b) Various techniques to avoid overfitting. (c) Different types of error measures and their suitability for different problems.

title: Out-of-Sample R-Squared Interpretation
statement: Statistics: Out-of-Sample R-squared. Explain the concept of out-of-sample R-squared. How can it be calculated, and what does it signify about a model's performance? Is it possible for the out-of-sample R-squared to be negative, and if so, what does that imply?

title: Sources of Bias in Regression Coefficients
statement: Statistics: Bias in Linear Regression Coefficients. Under what circumstances can the estimated coefficients ($\beta$) in a linear regression model be biased? Discuss sources of bias such as small sample size, model misspecification (e.g., omitted variables), and biased sampling methods.

title: Data Analysis Challenge with Interpolation
statement: Coding and Data Analysis Challenge. You are given a dataset in a DataFrame. (a) Implement linear interpolation for missing values. (b) Perform exploratory data analysis on the data. (c) Build a regression model to predict a target variable, justifying your choice of Mean Squared Error (MSE) as the loss function. (d) As a bonus, implement a feature selection method like forward selection to improve the model. The solution should use libraries like Pandas and Scikit-Learn and pass all provided test cases.

title: Duplicate Data Points Impact on Regression
statement: Statistics: Data Issues in Regression. When performing a linear regression, how would you handle the issue of duplicate data points in your dataset? Discuss the potential impact on model parameters and performance metrics.

title: Bash Script for Phone Number Extraction
statement: Coding: Bash Scripting. Write a bash script to find and extract valid phone numbers from a text file. This is LeetCode problem 193. The solution should be expressible using standard Unix tools like `grep`, `sed`, or `awk` with regular expressions.

title: Alternative Data Analysis for Retail Performance
statement: Case Study: Alternative Data Analysis. You are given a large consumer transaction dataset. (a) How would you use this data to analyze the business performance of Whole Foods after its acquisition by Amazon, compared to its performance before? (b) If you observe that Whole Foods' revenue is decreasing on the East Coast while increasing on the West Coast, what are the potential underlying reasons? Propose a method to investigate this using the given data, focusing on feature engineering.

title: Sample Size for Detecting a Biased Coin
statement: Statistics: Hypothesis Testing and Sample Size. How many coin flips (trials) would you need to be reasonably confident in distinguishing an unfair coin with a probability of heads $p=0.49$ from a fair coin ($p=0.5$)? Explain your reasoning, including the concepts of statistical power, significance level, and effect size.

title: Profitable Taxi Route Prediction Model
statement: Case Study: Modeling Profitable Taxi Routes. Given historical taxi trip data (including pickup/dropoff locations, times, fares, and tips), how would you design a model to predict the most profitable route or sequence of actions for a driver to take throughout the day? Discuss feature engineering, the choice of the target variable (e.g., profit per hour), and the modeling approach.

title: Symmetry in Simple Linear Regression
statement: Statistics: Symmetry in Linear Regression. (a) In simple linear regression, what is the relationship between the R-squared from regressing Y on X and the R-squared from regressing X on Y? (b) What is the relationship between their slope coefficients? Are they reciprocals of each other? (c) The standard OLS loss function is not symmetric with respect to X and Y. How can you define a loss function or use a method (like Principal Component Analysis) to find a symmetric "line of best fit"?

title: Difference of Geometric Brownian Motions
statement: Quantitative Finance: Difference of Geometric Brownian Motions. If two assets follow Geometric Brownian Motion (GBM), does the process representing the difference between their prices also follow a GBM? If not, why? Are there any special cases where it might hold or be simplified?

title: Probability: Distinct Outcomes in Dice Rolls
statement: Probability: Distinct Outcomes in Dice Rolls. A fair six-sided die is rolled six times. What is the probability of getting exactly four distinct numbers among the six outcomes?

title: Hash Map with Linear Probing
statement: CS Fundamentals: Hash Map with Linear Probing. (a) Explain the runtime complexity of operations in a hash map. (b) Explain how linear probing works as a collision resolution strategy. What are its advantages and disadvantages (e.g., clustering)?

title: Algorithm: External Sorting
statement: Algorithm: External Sorting. You need to sort 1TB of data, but you only have 1GB of available memory. Describe an algorithm to accomplish this. This is a classic external sorting problem.

title: Daily Median of Streaming Stock Prices
statement: Algorithm: Daily Median of Stock Prices. You are given a continuous stream of daily stock prices for $n$ stocks. Design an efficient algorithm to find the median price across all stocks for each day as a new day's prices arrive. Analyze the runtime complexity.

title: Impact of Adding Derived Features to Regression
statement: Statistics: Impact of Adding Derived Features to a Regression. Consider a linear regression model $y \sim x_1 + x_2 + x_3$. (a) Suppose you create a new variable $x_4 = x_3 - x_2$ and add it to the model, fitting $y \sim x_1 + x_2 + x_3 + x_4$. How would the model change (coefficients, standard errors, R-squared)? (b) What if you added $x_4 = x_3 \times x_2$ (an interaction term) instead? How would the R-squared change?

title: O(1) Push and Random Pop Data Structure
statement: Data Structure Design: O(1) Push and Random Pop. (a) Design a data structure that supports `push` (add an element) and `randomPop` (remove and return a random element) in O(1) time. (b) How would you modify your design if the elements had weights, and `randomPop` needed to be performed according to those weights?

title: Fixed-Size Container for First N Elements
statement: Data Structure Design: Fixed-Size Container for First N Elements. Design a data structure that receives a stream of elements. It should store the first 20 elements it receives and discard all subsequent elements. How can you optimize the `pop` operation for this structure?

title: Comparing Rolls of Different Sided Dice
statement: Probability: Comparing Rolls of Two Different Dice. You roll a 20-sided die and a 30-sided die. What is the probability that the number on the 30-sided die is strictly greater than the number on the 20-sided die?

title: Data Analysis Pipeline (Coding Problem)
statement: In a coding environment like Codepad, you are given a dataset. Perform a full data analysis pipeline using Python and pandas. This should include exploratory data analysis (EDA), such as checking feature types, scales, and for NaN values, and visualizing a correlation heatmap. Then, clean the data and implement a baseline linear regression model. The task emphasizes proficiency with the library without code completion tools.

title: Linear Regression Concepts
statement: Discuss the assumptions of linear regression and the issue of collinearity. How does collinearity affect the model's coefficients, their variance, and their interpretation?

title: Two Pointers (Coding Problem)
statement: Solve a classic LeetCode problem that uses the two-pointers technique. An example is finding pairs that sum to a target.

title: Optimal Estimate from Two Measurements
statement: You use two different scales to measure your weight. Assume the reading from scale $i$ follows a normal distribution $N(w, \sigma_i^2)$, where $w$ is your true weight. Given one reading from each scale, how do you combine these two measurements to get the most reliable estimate for $w$? Propose a method, such as Maximum Likelihood Estimation or minimum variance unbiased estimation, and derive the estimator.

title: Conditional Probability of Uniforms
statement: Let $X, Y, Z$ be i.i.d. random variables from a Uniform(0,1) distribution. Calculate the probability $P(\max\{X,Y,Z\} < 0.5 \mid X+Y+Z=1)$.

title: Option Pricing on a Dice Product
statement: The value of an underlying asset, $S$, is determined by the product of the outcomes of two independent 100-sided dice rolls. Calculate the fair price of a European call option with a strike price of K = 9700 that expires immediately.

title: Game Design to Minimize Loss
statement: You are designing a game. You have 100 cards, and you must assign a number from 1 to 5 to each card. An opponent will draw a card at random and guess the number on it. If they guess correctly, you must pay them an amount equal to that number. Assume the opponent knows the distribution of numbers you've chosen and will play optimally to maximize their winnings. How should you distribute the numbers on the cards to minimize your expected loss?

title: Betting Game Strategy
statement:
Players A and B play a game. Each antes \$1. They each draw a random number from U(0, 100). The player with the higher number wins the pot. The game proceeds in turns:
1. Player A acts first and can either 'check' or 'raise' by betting an additional \$2.
2. If A checks, B must also check, and they reveal their numbers.
3. If A raises, B can either 'fold' (losing their \$1 ante) or 'call' (matching the \$2 bet).
Describe the optimal strategy for player B, given player A's action and B's own number.

title: Effect of Duplicating Data on Regression
statement: You run a simple linear regression. Then, you create a new dataset by duplicating every data point from the original set. How do the following statistics change for the new regression: the slope coefficient, R-squared, and the t-statistic of the slope?

title: OLS Slopes of Y~X vs X~Y
statement: For a simple linear regression of Y on X, you get a slope $\beta_1$. For a regression of X on Y, you get $\beta_2$. What is the relationship between $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$? What is the range of their product, $\beta_1 \beta_2$?

title: Pirate Game and Coupon Collector's Problem
statement: Solve these two classic brain teasers from the "green book" (Heard on the Street): (a) The pirate game of distributing gold. (b) The coupon collector's problem.

title: Optimal Fibonacci Sequence (Coding Problem)
statement: Implement a function to compute the $n$-th Fibonacci number. Discuss different approaches and their time/space complexity, including the most optimal solution (e.g., matrix exponentiation for O(log n) time).

title: Design Tic-Tac-Toe (Coding Problem)
statement: Design and implement a Tic-Tac-Toe game on an $n \times n$ board. Your class should have a `move` method that takes a player and a position, and it should efficiently determine if that move results in a win. This corresponds to LeetCode 348.

title: Range of Equicorrelation
statement: For $n$ random variables, if the correlation between any two distinct variables is $\rho$, what is the possible range for $\rho$?

title: "Guess 2/3 of the Average" Game
statement: In a game, $n$ people each write down an integer between 1 and 100. The winner is the person whose number is closest to 2/3 of the average of all numbers submitted. What is the Nash equilibrium strategy?

title: Max Drawdown (Coding Problem)
statement: Given a time series of asset prices, calculate the maximum drawdown, which is the maximum loss from a peak to a trough. This corresponds to LeetCode 121, Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock.

title: Optimization of Quadratic Form
statement: Find the maximum of the quadratic form $x^T A x$ for a vector $x$, where $A$ is a square matrix. Consider the cases where $A$ is symmetric and not symmetric.

title: Uniform Sampling from a Solid Disk
statement: Describe an algorithm to sample points uniformly from the interior of a unit disk. Why is simply sampling radius and angle uniformly incorrect? Provide the correct method.

title: Optimal Step Function Fitting (Coding Problem)
statement: Given $n$ data points $(x_i, y_i)$, you want to fit a function composed of $k$ step functions to this data. Describe an optimal algorithm to find the step function parameters that minimize the sum of squared errors. (Hint: This can be solved with dynamic programming).

title: Expectation of Maximum of Uniforms
statement: Let $X, Y \stackrel{i.i.d.}{\sim} U[0,1]$. Calculate $E[\max(X, Y)]$. Follow-up: For $n$ i.i.d. variables, what is $E[X_{(n)}]$?

title: Maximum Drawdown in a Sliding Window (Coding Problem)
statement: Given a time series of prices and a window size $k$, find the maximum drawdown within each sliding window. This is a harder variation of LeetCode 121 and 239.

title: Numerical Function Minimization (Coding Problem)
statement: Write a function that takes an arbitrary mathematical function $f(x)$ as its argument and finds a value $x$ that minimizes $f(x)$. You should implement a numerical solution, such as gradient descent. Discuss how you would approximate the derivative.

title: Sum and Independence of Gaussian Variables
statement: Let $X, Y$ be standard Gaussian random variables. (a) Is the sum $X+Y$ also Gaussian? (b) What is the relationship between independence and uncorrelatedness for $X$ and $Y$?

title: Negative R-squared
statement: Is it possible for the R-squared value in a linear regression to be negative? If so, under what circumstances?

title: Find Geometric Median (Coding Problem)
statement: Given a set of points in a 2D plane, find their geometric median: the point that minimizes the sum of Euclidean distances to all other points. Implement a solution using (sub)gradient descent. This corresponds to LeetCode 1515.

title: Annualizing Sharpe Ratio
statement: How do you convert a daily Sharpe ratio to an annualized Sharpe ratio? What is the justification for the standard multiplier?

title: Recursive Least Squares
statement: How can you update the coefficients of a linear regression model in an online manner as new data arrives? Describe the Recursive Least Squares (RLS) algorithm.

title: LFU Cache (Coding Problem)
statement: Design and implement a data structure for a Least Frequently Used (LFU) cache. This corresponds to LeetCode 460.

title: Square Root of a Float (Coding Problem)
statement: Implement `sqrt(x)` for a floating-point number `x`, returning the result with a specified accuracy (e.g., using Newton's method). This corresponds to LeetCode 69.

title: Rolling Rank in a Window (Coding Problem)
statement: You are given a list of numbers and a rolling window of size $K$. For each window, compute the rank of the newest element within that window's elements.

title: The Umbrella Problem (Markov Chain)
statement: A professor owns $n$ umbrellas and commutes between home and office. On each trip, it rains with probability $p$. If it is raining, they take an umbrella if one is available. If not, they get wet. What is the expected number of trips until the professor first gets wet?

title: Edit Distance (Coding Problem)
statement: Given two words, find the minimum number of operations (insert, delete, substitute) required to convert one to the other. This is LeetCode 72.

title: Uniform Sampling from a Sphere's Surface
statement: How do you uniformly sample a point from the surface of a 3D unit sphere? Describe a correct method, such as using three standard normal variables.

title: List of LeetCode Coding Problems
statement:
Be prepared for a variety of LeetCode problems, often with a quantitative or statistical flavor. Commonly cited problems include:

    
- LC 23: Merge K Sorted Lists
    
- LC 42: Trapping Rain Water (and variations)
    
- LC 53: Maximum Subarray
    
- LC 200: Number of Islands
    
- LC 239: Sliding Window Maximum
    
- LC 300: Longest Increasing Subsequence
    
- LC 370: Range Addition
    
- LC 560: Subarray Sum Equals K
    
- LC 767: Reorganize String
    
- LC 986: Interval List Intersections

title: Random Walk Problems
statement:
(a) What is the expected time for a 1D random walk to exit a given interval?
(b) What is the expected time for a random walk on a circle of N nodes to visit every node (cover time)?

title: Advanced Regression Topics
statement:
(a) For Ridge regression, what data preprocessing is necessary? Are the residuals orthogonal to the predicted values?
(b) Given Corr(Y, X1) > 0, Corr(Y, X2) = 0, Corr(X1, X2) > 0. Compare the coefficients of X1 in the regressions Y ~ X1 and Y ~ X1 + X2.
(c) Explain stationarity in time series. Why is it important?

title: Bayesian Modeling of Rare Events
statement: Design a Bayesian model for the probability of a rare event. What would you choose for your prior distribution? How would you parameterize the likelihood? How would you derive the posterior?

title: Finance and Trading Questions
statement:
(a) Discuss execution risk in pairs trading.
(b) What are potential issues with estimating correlation using high-frequency data?
(c) How can you neutralize an alpha strategy against a set of risk factors?
(d) In portfolio optimization, how do you avoid breaking cross-sectional neutrality?

title: Ranking Guessing Game
statement: You are shown $n$ i.i.d. random variables from U(0,1) one by one. After seeing each variable $x_i$, you must guess its rank among all $n$ variables. You win only if you guess every rank correctly. What is your best strategy and what is the probability of winning?

title: Biased Coin for a Fair Game
statement: You have a biased coin with an unknown probability of heads. How can you use it to simulate a fair coin toss? What is the expected number of tosses required per fair outcome?

title: Pancake Sorting Variation
statement: You have a stack of pancakes of different sizes. The only allowed operation is to insert a spatula at any point in the stack and flip the portion of the stack above the spatula. How can you sort the pancakes from largest at the bottom to smallest at the top?

title: Probability of No HH
statement: What is the probability of not seeing the pattern "HH" in N tosses of a fair coin?

title: Online Mean and Standard Deviation
statement: Design an algorithm to compute the mean and standard deviation of a data stream in a single pass (online manner).

title: Bayesian Inference with a Bad Coin
statement: You have 1000 coins, one of which is a "bad coin" that always lands heads. The other 999 are fair. You pick a coin at random and flip it 10 times, getting 10 heads. What is the probability you picked the bad coin?

title: Sort by Encounter Order
statement: Sort a list of items such that identical items are grouped together, but the groups appear in the order of their first appearance in the original list. Example: [1,3,1,5,1,4,4,7] -> [1,1,1,3,5,4,4,7].

title: Point in Triangle (Coding Problem)
statement: Given the coordinates of a triangle's three vertices and the coordinates of a point P, determine if P is inside the triangle.

title: Trie for Prefix Search (Coding Problem)
statement: Given a list of words, design a data structure (e.g., a Trie) to efficiently return all words that start with a given prefix.

title: Biased Sampling
statement: To estimate the average number of residents per building in a city, you sample 100 people on the street and ask how many people live in their building. Why is the sample average a biased estimator? What is the correct way to estimate the true average (e.g., using the harmonic mean)?

title: Expectation of a Function of a Random Variable
statement: Given a random variable $S$, its expectation $E[S]$, and the values of European call and put options $E[\max(S-K, 0)]$ and $E[\max(K-S, 0)]$ for any strike $K$. Find an expression for $E[f(S)]$ where $f$ is an arbitrary twice-differentiable function. (Hint: Carr-Madan formula / Breeden-Litzenberger identity).

title: Median Regression
statement: What is median regression (e.g., Least Absolute Deviations)? In what situations is it preferable to OLS (e.g., presence of outliers, heavy-tailed errors)? Why is OLS more commonly used?

title: Vector Projection
statement: Given two n-dimensional vectors $p$ and $\beta$, find the vector closest to $p$ that is also orthogonal to $\beta$.

title: Queue with Get-Max in O(1) (Coding Problem)
statement: Implement a queue data structure that supports the standard `enqueue` and `dequeue` operations, as well as a `get_max` operation, all in O(1) amortized time.

title: Correlation of a Sum
statement: Given random variables $H, X, Y$, and known correlations $\text{corr}(H, X)$ and $\text{corr}(H, Y)$, what can you say about $\text{corr}(H, X+Y)$?

title: Dice Game Expectation
statement:
Two games are available:
1. Roll two fair six-sided dice. Your payoff is the product of the outcomes.
2. Roll one fair six-sided die. Your payoff is the square of the outcome.
Which game has a higher expected payoff? Answer this intuitively without calculation, then verify with calculation.

title: Expected Adjacent Different Color Cards
statement: You have a shuffled deck of $n$ white cards and $n$ black cards. What is the expected number of adjacent pairs of cards that have different colors?

title: Probability and Option Payoff Questions
statement:
(a) Roll a 10-sided die and a 20-sided die. What's the probability the 10-sided die's outcome is greater?
(b) What is the expected number of rolls of an 8-sided die to get two 8s in a row?
(c) In a best-of-7 series where both teams have a 50% chance of winning each game, what is the probability the series goes to 7 games?
(d) What is the expected number of cards you need to draw from a 52-card deck to have seen at least one of each of the four suits?
(e) You are offered a zero-premium, out-of-the-money call option with a delta of 30. Would you buy it? Discuss hedging strategies and associated risks.

title: Loss Functions and Estimators
statement:
(a) Find $\arg\min_y \sum_i(x_i - y)^2$. (Answer: mean)
(b) Find $\arg\min_y \sum_i|x_i - y|$. (Answer: median)

title: Machine Learning General Questions
statement:
(a) How does PCA work? If you add a feature to your dataset, how does the variance explained by the first principal component change?
(b) Compare Random Forest and Gradient Boosting. Why can't you use strong learners in boosting?
(c) Why do we use non-linear activation functions in neural networks?
(d) If training accuracy is high but test accuracy is low, what do you do? Discuss regularization (L1/L2), data augmentation, etc.

title: C++ Class Design: Coordinates and Hashing
statement:
Design a C++ class for a point in a 2D plane. The class should support:
(a) Representation in both Cartesian (x, y) and Polar (r, $\theta$) coordinates, with methods to convert between them.
(b) The ability for objects of this class to be stored in `std::set` and `std::unordered_set`. What member functions must you implement or overload to achieve this (e.g., comparison operators, hash functions)?

title: Maximum Points in an Angle (Geometric Algorithm)
statement: Given a set of points in a 2D plane and an angle $\alpha$, find the rotation of the angle (centered at the origin) that allows it to contain the maximum number of points.

title: Combinatorics: Stars and Bars
statement: Solve a combinatorial problem using the "stars and bars" method. For example, how many ways are there to distribute $n$ identical items into $k$ distinct bins?

title: PCA Variance with an Additional Feature
statement: You perform Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on a dataset. If you add a new feature to this dataset, will the variance explained by the new first principal component be greater than, less than, or equal to the variance explained by the old first principal component? Prove your answer.

title: Magic Square (Coding Problem)
statement: Write a function to determine if a given $N \times N$ matrix is a magic square. A magic square contains the integers from 1 to $N^2$ exactly once, and the sum of the integers in each row, each column, and both main diagonals is the same.

title: Generate Permutations and Combinations (Coding Problem)
statement: Without using built-in library functions like `itertools.permutations`, write functions to: (a) Generate all permutations of a given list of unique elements. (b) Generate all combinations of size $k$ from a given list.

title: Find Primes up to N (Coding Problem)
statement: Implement an efficient algorithm, such as the Sieve of Eratosthenes, to find all prime numbers up to a given integer $n$. Analyze its time complexity.

title: Two Envelopes Paradox
statement: Explain the Two Envelopes Paradox. A player is presented with two envelopes, one containing twice as much money as the other. The player picks one, opens it, and sees some amount $X$. They are then offered the chance to switch to the other envelope. The standard argument suggests switching is always beneficial. Explain why this reasoning is flawed.

title: N Points in a Semicircle
statement: If you pick $n$ points uniformly at random on the circumference of a circle, what is the probability that they all lie within some semicircle?

title: Case Study: Experiment Design for Policy Impact
statement: A new policy has been implemented (e.g., a new feature on a website). How would you design an experiment to determine if the policy is effective? Discuss what data you would need, your methodology (e.g., A/B testing), how you would measure success, and what statistical pitfalls could affect your conclusion.

title: Probability of Strictly Increasing Dice Rolls
statement: If four fair six-sided dice are rolled, what is the probability that the outcomes are strictly increasing?

title: Dimensionality Reduction Concepts
statement: Given a high-dimensional $N \times P$ data matrix (where $P \gg N$), how would you approach dimensionality reduction? Discuss this from a linear algebra perspective, touching upon concepts like rank, image, orthogonality, and the Gram-Schmidt process.

title: Conditional Probability of Arrivals
statement: Three people fly from city A, two from B, and one from C. Their arrival order at the destination airport is completely random. What is the probability that when the person from C arrives, at least one person from A and at least one person from B have not yet arrived?

title: Machine Learning Concepts
statement: Explain the following concepts: (a) The difference between Gradient Boosting and Random Forests. (b) The intuition behind batch normalization in deep learning. (c) The intuition behind using momentum in stochastic gradient descent.

title: Case Study: Feature Selection with Many Features
statement: You are building a model with 10 features. You have a pool of 1 million candidate features to add. You test them one by one, and none seem to improve the model until the very last one provides a significant lift. How would you interpret this? What are your next steps to ensure this is a robust finding and not a result of multiple testing fallacy?

title: Ridge Regression for Time Series
statement:
Consider using Ridge regression for a time-series prediction task.
(a) How would you expect the optimal regularization parameter $\lambda$ to change if you add more independent features to the model? What if you add more correlated features?
(b) How would the optimal $\lambda$ differ between two scenarios: (i) sampling data every 1 second, and (ii) sampling data every 10 seconds?

title: Maximum Product Cutting (Coding Problem)
statement: Given a rope of length $n$, find the maximum product you can get by cutting the rope into integer-length pieces.

title: HTH vs HTT Game (Probability)
statement: Alice and Bob toss a fair coin repeatedly. Alice wins if the sequence HTH appears first. Bob wins if HTT appears first. What is the probability that Alice wins?

title: Distributed OLS Computation
statement: What is the closed-form solution for OLS? If the data matrix is too large to fit in memory (e.g., many samples), how can you compute the OLS solution? (Hint: Consider the dimensions of $X^TX$).

title: Regularization and Prediction Horizon
statement: A neural network is trained to predict a car's position 1 second ahead and 10 seconds ahead. Which prediction task requires stronger regularization and why? Are there alternative ways to improve the long-horizon prediction without using regularization?

title: System Design and Multithreading Questions
statement:
(a) You are given a binary matrix where a "duck" shape is represented by 1s. Given a starting point inside the duck, write a multithreaded algorithm to flip all 1s inside the duck to 0s.
(b) How would you optimize a Fibonacci function for sparse, random inputs (i.e., make repeated calls efficient)?
(c) Design a high-level architecture for a system that stores and retrieves large-scale financial market data for quantitative modeling.

title: Game Theory: Tic-Tac-Toe Expected Value
statement: You play a game where 3 pieces are placed randomly on a 3x3 tic-tac-toe board. If the pieces form a line (a "tic-tac-toe"), you win \$9. Otherwise, you lose \$1. Should you play this game? Calculate the expected value.

title: Optimal Strategy for a Card Game
statement: You are presented with three face-down cards with unknown integer values $n, n+1, n+2$. You can flip one card. You may either "stay" and accept its value as your payoff, or discard it and flip a second card. You may again "stay" with the second card's value, or you must take the value of the third (last) card. What is the optimal strategy to maximize your expected payoff?

title: Numerically Stable Online Statistics
statement: Design a class or algorithm to compute the mean and standard deviation of a data stream in a single pass. Discuss potential numerical stability issues with the naive variance formula and how to address them (e.g., using Welford's algorithm).

title: The k-th "3-Smooth" Number (Coding Problem)
statement: A number is "3-smooth" if its only prime factors are 2, 3, and 5 (these are also called Hamming numbers or ugly numbers). Write an efficient algorithm to find the $k$-th largest number of this type.

title: Rope Linking Expectation
statement: You have $N$ ropes, each of length 1. At each step, you randomly pick two free rope ends (with probability proportional to the length of the ropes they are attached to) and tie them together. This process continues until no free ends are left, forming one or more loops. What is the expected number of loops? How does this number relate to $N$? (Hint: Consider the Harmonic series).

title: Card Game Probability
statement: From a shuffled 52-card deck, you turn over cards one by one. Which of the following events is more likely to happen first: (a) you see a second Ace (after the first one has already appeared), or (b) you see the Two of Spades?

title: Two Players Guessing Coin Flips
statement: Alice and Bob want to win a game where they must both correctly guess the outcome of a future coin flip. Before the flip, they can agree on a strategy. Alice is then told the result of the flip in advance, but Bob is not. Alice can then send a single bit of information to Bob (e.g., say "heads" or "tails"). What strategy gives them a probability of winning greater than 1/2?

title: MLE of Uniform Distribution Parameter
statement: Given $n$ i.i.d. samples from a Uniform(0, $\theta$) distribution, derive the Maximum Likelihood Estimator (MLE) for $\theta$. Is this estimator unbiased?

title: 24 Game (Coding Problem)
statement: Given four numbers, determine if you can obtain the value 24 using the operations +, -, *, / and parentheses. The problem can be extended to handle fractions and negative numbers.

title: Large Integer Sum with Constant Space (Coding Problem)
statement: You are given two large integers, represented as streams of digits of equal length. Process the digits one by one (one from each integer) from left to right and output the digits of their sum. Your algorithm must use only O(1) extra space.

title: Generate Balanced Parentheses (Coding Problem)
statement: Given $n$ pairs of parentheses, write a function to generate all combinations of well-formed parentheses. This is LeetCode 22.

title: Covariance Bounds
statement: Given Corr(A, B) = 0.5 and Corr(B, C) = 0.5, what is the possible range for Corr(A, C)? What property of the covariance matrix must hold? (Hint: Semidefinite).

title: Average Stock Holding Time (Coding Problem)
statement: You are given a log of buy and sell transactions for a single stock for one day. The log consists of (quantity, time) tuples, where positive quantity is a buy and negative is a sell. The net position starts and ends at zero. Define and implement an algorithm to calculate the average holding time for a share of the stock.

title: Optimal Stopping: Red vs Black Card Game
statement: You play a game with a standard 52-card deck. Cards are turned over one by one. For each red card, you win \$1. For each black card, you lose \$1. You can choose to stop the game at any time. What is the optimal strategy and what is your expected winning?

title: PDF of a Sum of Uniforms
statement: If $X$ and $Y$ are i.i.d. random variables from a Uniform(0,1) distribution, what is the probability density function (PDF) of their sum, $Z = X+Y$?

title: Eigenvalues of an Equicorrelated Matrix
statement: Find the eigenvalues of an $n \times n$ matrix where the diagonal elements are all 1 and all off-diagonal elements are equal to $\rho$.

title: System Design: Trading Platform
statement: Design a simplified limit order book for a trading platform. It should support adding, removing, and modifying limit orders, and processing market orders that execute against the book.

title: World Series Problem (Dynamic Programming)
statement: Two teams play a best-of-seven series (first to win 4 games wins). Team A has a probability $p$ of winning any given game. What is the probability that team A wins the series? What is the expected number of games played?

title: Distributed Merge Sort
statement: Describe how you would implement merge sort if the array is too large to fit on a single machine and is distributed across several machines. Analyze the computation and communication costs.

title: OLS Confidence Intervals
statement: How do you derive the confidence interval for a coefficient in a simple linear regression model? What assumptions are needed?

title: Case Study: Mining Credit Card Data
statement: You are given a massive dataset of credit card transactions, including time, location, merchant, and amount. What kind of valuable information could you extract from this data to generate a profit (e.g., for trading, market research, etc.)?

title: Regression with Leverage Points
statement: In a simple linear regression, what is a leverage point? How does adding a leverage point affect the regression line? How can you make your regression model more robust to such points?

title: Model Comparison: Logistic vs. Linear vs. SVM
statement: Compare and contrast Logistic Regression, Linear Regression, and Support Vector Machines (SVMs). When would you choose one over the others?

title: Generating Normal from Uniform
statement: Describe a method (e.g., the Box-Muller transform) for generating standard normal random variables using a generator for Uniform(0,1) variables.

title: Case Study: MVO from a Linear Algebra Perspective
statement: Discuss Mean-Variance Optimization (MVO) for portfolios from a linear algebra perspective. What are the inputs and outputs? How do you solve the constrained optimization problem?

title: Egg Dropping Puzzle (Dynamic Programming)
statement: You have $k$ eggs and a building with $n$ floors. Find the minimum number of drops required in the worst case to determine the highest floor from which an egg will not break.

title: Polya's Urn Model
statement: A basketball player has made $m$ shots out of $n$ attempts so far. Their probability of making the next shot is given by $m/n$. If they start with 1 successful shot out of 2 attempts, what is the distribution of the number of successful shots after 100 total attempts?

title: Regression with d > n
statement: What are the problems with performing OLS regression when the number of features $d$ is greater than the number of data points $n$? What are some solutions (e.g., Ridge, Lasso, PCA)?

title: Generate 1-7 from 1-5 Random Generator
statement: Given a function that generates a random integer from 1 to 5 uniformly, write a function that generates a random integer from 1 to 7 uniformly.

title: Decode Number String (Coding Problem)
statement: Given a mapping 'a' -> 1, 'b' -> 2, ..., 'z' -> 26, and a string of digits, count the number of ways it can be decoded. For example, "123" can be "abc", "lc", or "aw".

title: Cross-Entropy and Jensen's Inequality
statement: Write down the formula for cross-entropy between two distributions $p(x)$ and $q(x)$. Explain what each part represents. How can Jensen's inequality be used to show that KL divergence (related to cross-entropy) is non-negative?

title: Extremum of $f(x)=x^x$
statement: Find the minimum value of the function $f(x)=x^x$ on the interval $(0, 1]$. What is the limit of $f(x)$ as $x \to 0^+$?

title: Biased Coin Comparison Game
statement: You are given two coins, A and B, which may be biased. You have 100 total flips to determine which coin has a higher probability of heads. How do you design your experiment (i.e., how many times to flip each coin) to maximize your confidence in the conclusion?

title: Angle Between y and y-hat in Ridge Regression
statement: In a linear regression model $y = X\beta + \epsilon$, prove or disprove the statement: For any choice of the L2 regularization parameter $\lambda > 0$, the angle between the observation vector $y$ and the predicted vector $\hat{y}_{\text{ridge}}$ is the same.

title: St. Petersburg Paradox
statement: Explain the St. Petersburg paradox. A fair coin is tossed until a head appears. If this happens on the $n$-th toss, the payoff is $\$2^n$. What is the expected payoff? How much would you be willing to pay to play this game? Discuss the implications for utility theory.

title: Auction Theory Bidding Strategy
statement: In a first-price sealed-bid auction, an item's value to you is uniformly distributed between \$0 and \$1M. Other bidders have their own valuations. You can sell the item on a secondary market for twice its value to you. What is your optimal bidding strategy?

title: Two Sum Count (Coding Problem)
statement: Given an array of integers and a target value, find the number of unique pairs of elements that sum up to the target.

title: Online Fraud Detection
statement: Describe how you would design an online (real-time) algorithm to detect fraudulent transactions (e.g., for Amazon orders). What features would you use? What models? How would you handle the class imbalance?

title: Deliver N Numbers as 1
statement: Alice has an array of $N$ decimal numbers she wants to send to Bob. How can she encode this entire array into a single number to send to Bob, such that Bob can perfectly reconstruct the original array?

title: Inverting a High-Dimensional Covariance Matrix
statement: Discuss numerical methods and challenges for inverting a high-dimensional covariance matrix, especially if it is ill-conditioned.

title: Simulating Correlated Random Variables
statement: Given a random number generator for a 1D standard normal distribution, how would you simulate three 3D random variables with a given mean vector and covariance matrix?

title: GARCH Model
statement: What is a GARCH model? What is it used for in finance? What phenomena does it capture that simpler models do not?

title: Variance of a Coordinate on a Sphere
statement: If you randomly pick a point $(x, y, z)$ from the surface of a sphere with radius $R$ centered at the origin, what is the variance of the $x$-coordinate?

title: Posterior Probability for Binomial Rates
statement: You have two unfair coins with head probabilities $p_1$ and $p_2$. You toss the first three times and get 2 heads. You toss the second three times and get 1 head. Assuming a uniform prior on $p_1$ and $p_2$, what is the posterior probability that $p_1 > p_2$?

title: Blind Coin Flipping Puzzle
statement: There are $N$ coins on a table, $k$ of which are heads up. You are blindfolded. Your goal is to make a move (flipping some coins) that guarantees all coins are in the same state (all heads or all tails). You are told the value of $k$ in advance. Can you find a strategy?

title: Pairwise vs. Joint Independence
statement: Provide a classic example of three random variables that are pairwise independent but not jointly independent.

title: Integral of a Gaussian
statement: What is the value of the integral $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-x^2} dx$? How is it derived?

title: Sum of Powers
statement: Discuss methods for finding a closed-form expression for the sum of powers, $\sum_{i=1}^{N} i^k$, for integer $k \ge 1$.

title: Standard Deviation of a Sum of Correlated Gaussians
statement: Let $X, Y \sim N(0,1)$ be two standard normal random variables. They are not necessarily independent. What is the possible range for the standard deviation of their sum, $Z = X+Y$?

title: Machine Learning: Kernel Methods and Gaussian Processes
statement:
(a) What are kernel methods in machine learning? What is the main advantage of using a kernelized version of an algorithm like SVM compared to its non-kernelized counterpart?
(b) Explain what a Gaussian Process is at a high level.

title: Reinforcement Learning: Q-Learning vs. Policy Gradients
statement: What are the main differences between Q-learning and Policy Gradient methods in reinforcement learning? Discuss their objectives, what they learn (value function vs. policy), and their relative advantages.

title: Online Sampling from a Stream
statement:
You are given a stream of data of unknown length.
(a) How do you randomly sample one element from the stream such that at any point, every element seen so far has an equal probability of being the chosen one? (Reservoir Sampling for k=1).
(b) How do you extend this to randomly sample a permutation of the stream?

title: Monte Carlo Estimation
statement: Describe how you would use the Monte Carlo method to estimate the value of (a) $\pi$ and (b) $e$.

title: Coding: Online Covariance and Correlation
statement: Write a class in a language of your choice that can process a stream of pairs of numbers $(x, y)$. It should have methods to update its internal state with a new pair and to calculate the current covariance and correlation between the X and Y streams. The implementation should not use any external numerical libraries.

title: Regression: Features vs. Data Points
statement: In a linear regression model, what problems arise as the number of features $p$ approaches the number of data points $n$? Is there a rule of thumb for a reasonable maximum number of features for a given $n$ to avoid overfitting?

title: Probability: The Gambler's Ruin
statement: A gambler starts with an initial fortune of $i$ dollars. On each bet, they win \$1 with probability $p$ and lose \$1 with probability $1-p$. The game stops when the gambler's fortune reaches $N$ or 0. What is the probability that the gambler's fortune reaches $N$ (i.e., they win)?

title: Data Structure: N-th Smallest in a Stream
statement: Design a data structure that supports two operations: `add(number)` to add a number to the collection, and `query(n)` to find the n-th smallest number currently in the collection. Discuss the trade-offs in time complexity for these two operations.

title: Finance: Backtesting and Transaction Costs
statement: When backtesting a trading strategy, why is it crucial to account for transaction costs? What are different types of transaction costs, and how would you model them?

title: Statistics: Best Linear Unbiased Estimator (BLUE)
statement: You have multiple unbiased estimators for the same parameter. How can you combine them using a weighted average to form a new estimator that is also unbiased and has the minimum possible variance? Derive the optimal weights.

title: Coding: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
statement: Given two sorted arrays, `nums1` and `nums2`, of size $m$ and $n$ respectively, find the median of the two sorted arrays. The overall run time complexity should be $O(\log(m+n))$. This is LeetCode problem 4.

title: Algorithm: Approximate Online Median
statement: For a continuous stream of numbers, describe an algorithm to compute an approximate median. The algorithm should use limited memory. Discuss the properties of the algorithm, such as whether it can produce the exact median and its percentile guarantees.

title: Coding: DP on a Grid - Random Walk Probability
statement: A particle starts at position $(x, y)$ on a grid from $(0,0)$ to $(7,7)$. In each step, it moves to one of the four adjacent squares with equal probability. What is the probability that the particle stays within the grid boundaries for $n$ steps? Describe a dynamic programming approach to solve this.

title: Statistics: Conditional Expectation of Multivariate Normal
statement: Given two jointly normal random variables $X$ and $Y$ with a known mean vector and covariance matrix, what is the expected value of $Y$ given that you observe $X=x$?

title: Machine Learning: PCA vs. Autoencoder
statement: Compare and contrast Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Autoencoders as dimensionality reduction techniques. When might one be preferred over the other?

title: Machine Learning: Regularization Concepts
statement:
(a) What is $L_0$ regularization, and what are the practical difficulties in using it?
(b) Provide an intuitive (e.g., geometric) explanation for why $L_1$ regularization (Lasso) tends to produce sparse solutions (many zero coefficients), while $L_2$ regularization (Ridge) does not.

title: Math: Limit of Fibonacci Ratio
statement: Without using the closed-form solution (Binet's formula) for Fibonacci numbers, prove that the limit of the ratio of successive terms, $\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{F_{n+1}}{F_n}$, exists and find its value.

title: Coding: K-th Most Frequent Number
statement: Given an array of integers, find the $k$-th most frequent element.

title: C++ unordered_map Default Value Behavior
statement: In C++, if you access a key in an `std::unordered\_map` that does not exist using the `[]` operator (e.g., `my\_map[key]++`), the map creates a new element. What are the requirements on the key and value types for this operation to be valid?

title: Coding: Numbers with Distinct Digits
statement: Given an integer $n$, count the number of positive integers with unique digits that are less than or equal to $n$.

title: Probability: The Secretary Problem
statement: Describe the Secretary Problem (or Marriage Problem). What is the optimal strategy for maximizing the probability of selecting the best candidate, and what is this probability as the number of candidates goes to infinity?

title: Statistics: Effect of Noise on Predictors in OLS
statement: In a simple linear regression $Y = \beta X + \epsilon$, what happens to the estimate of $\beta$ if the predictor $X$ is measured with error? That is, you observe $X^* = X + \eta$ and regress $Y$ on $X^*$. How does this relate to regularization?

title: Algorithm: Quickselect
statement: Describe the Quickselect algorithm for finding the $k$-th smallest element in an unordered list. What is its average and worst-case time complexity?

title: Statistics: Stationarity and Residual Autocorrelation
statement:
(a) How do you test if a time series is stationary?
(b) After fitting a time series model (like ARMA), you find that the residuals are autocorrelated. What does this imply about your model, and what are the next steps?

title: Finance: The Kelly Criterion
statement: What is the Kelly Criterion? Explain its purpose in betting and investment sizing.

title: Python Fundamentals
statement:
(a) What is a generator in Python? How is it different from a list comprehension?
(b) What are the main differences between Python's `tuple`, `list`, and `dict` data types in terms of mutability, ordering, and use cases?

title: Probability: Bayesian Detector Accuracy
statement: A medical test for a disease is 95\% accurate (i.e., if a person has the disease, it tests positive 95\% of the time; if they don't, it tests negative 95\% of the time). The disease has a prevalence of 1 in 1000 people. If a randomly selected person tests positive, what is the probability they actually have the disease?

title: C++: Initializing Reference Members
statement: In a C++ class, how must you initialize a reference member variable? Why can't it be assigned in the constructor body?

title: Coding: Reverse Words in a String
statement: Given an input string, reverse the string word by word in-place. For example, ``hello world'' becomes ``world hello''.

title: Finance: One-Step Binomial Option Pricing
statement: Explain how to price a European call option using a one-step binomial model. Define the risk-neutral probability and the replication portfolio.

title: Linear Algebra: Positive Definite Matrix
statement: What are some ways to check if a symmetric matrix (like a covariance matrix) is positive definite?

title: Statistics: OLS with Non-linear Data
statement: You run an OLS regression of $Y$ on $X$. What is the expected value of the slope coefficient if the true relationship is (a) $Y = X^2 + \epsilon$, or (b) $Y = X^3 + \epsilon$? Assume $X \sim N(0,1)$ and $\epsilon \sim N(0,1)$ is independent of $X$.

title: Probability: Conditional Bernoulli Sums
statement: Let $X_1, \dots, X_{100}$ be i.i.d. Bernoulli$(p)$ random variables. What is the conditional probability $P(X_1=1 \mid \sum_{i=1}^{100} X_i = 20)$?

title: Coding: Implement Quicksort
statement: Write a function that implements the Quicksort algorithm.

title: Coding: Count of Target in Sorted Array
statement: Given a sorted array of integers, find the number of occurrences of a given target value. The solution should be more efficient than a linear scan.

title: Statistics: Generalized Linear Models (GLM)
statement: What is a Generalized Linear Model (GLM)? How does it extend ordinary linear regression? Give an example, like Poisson regression.

title: Coding: Univalued Binary Tree
statement: Determine if a binary tree is univalued, meaning all nodes in the tree have the same value. This is LeetCode problem 965.

title: Algorithm: Master Theorem
statement: What is the Master Theorem used for? State its three main cases for solving recurrence relations of the form $T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n)$.

title: Puzzle: Balance Scale and Weights
statement: You have a balance scale and a set of weights. How can you weigh any integer amount from 1 to 40 pounds using the minimum number of weights? (Hint: Weights can be placed on either side of the scale).

title: Puzzle: Flipping Cups Invariant
statement: Four cups are placed at the corners of a square table. You are blindfolded. Your goal is to get all cups facing the same way (up or down). In each move, you can choose any two cups and flip them over. After your move, the table may be rotated by an unknown amount. Is there a winning strategy?

title: Probability: Expectation of Minimum of Uniforms
statement: Let $A \sim U(0,5)$ and $B \sim U(0,10)$ be independent. Calculate $E[\min(A,B)].$

title: Puzzle: Non-standard Dice Sum
statement: The sum of two standard six-sided dice follows a specific distribution. Is it possible to design a pair of non-standard six-sided dice (with positive integer faces) whose sum has the exact same distribution? These are known as Sicherman dice.

title: Probability: Random Partitioning Game
statement: You start with a set of $n$ items. At each step, you randomly partition the current sets of items into two non-empty subsets. For each partition of a set of size $k$ into subsets of size $k_1$ and $k_2$, you score $k_1 \times k_2$ points. The process continues until all items are in sets of size 1. What is the total score? (Hint: The result is deterministic).

title: Coding: Database Outer Join
statement: Describe how a database LEFT OUTER JOIN works. Given two tables as lists of tuples, implement a function to perform a left outer join.

title: Probability: Dice Roll Comparison
statement: You roll two fair six-sided dice. What is the probability that the outcome of the second die is strictly less than the outcome of the first?

title: Probability: Conditional Expectation Game
statement: You roll a fair six-sided die repeatedly. If the outcome is 4, 5, or 6, you get paid that amount and the game continues. If the outcome is 1, 2, or 3, you get paid that amount and the game stops. What is the expected total payoff?

title: Algorithm: Online Outlier Detection
statement: Describe a simple algorithm for online outlier detection in a stream of 1D data. Define what you consider an outlier and justify your method (e.g., based on a running mean and standard deviation).

title: Statistics: Comparison of Estimators
statement: For a sample from a $U(0, \theta)$ distribution, compare the Mean Squared Error (MSE) of two estimators for the mean, $\theta/2$: (a) the sample mean, and (b) half the sample maximum.

title: AI: Tic-Tac-Toe AI
statement: Describe how you would implement an AI to play Tic-Tac-Toe. Discuss strategies like minimax and potential optimizations.

title: Coding: k-Means Clustering
statement: Implement the k-means clustering algorithm from scratch.

title: C++: Compiler-Generated Class Methods
statement: If you define an empty class in C++, `class A \{\`;}, what member functions will the compiler typically generate for you by default?

title: Math: Riccati Differential Equation
statement: What is a Riccati equation? Describe a general form and discuss its properties or methods of solution.

title: Expectation of Ratio of Uniforms
statement: Let $X, Y \stackrel{i.i.d.}{\sim} U[1,3]$. Compute $E[X/Y]$.

title: Stationary Distribution of a Markov Chain
statement: Consider a system with $n$ states and a given transition matrix $P$. For example, state 1 has a 1/2 probability of remaining in state 1 and a 1/2 probability of transitioning to state 2; state 2 has a 1/2 probability of remaining, a 1/4 probability of transitioning to state 1, and a 1/4 probability of transitioning to state 3, etc. What is the long-run fraction of time that the system spends in state 1? This is equivalent to finding the stationary distribution of the Markov chain.

title: Probability of a Symmetric Random Binary Tree
statement: Consider a random binary tree where each node independently decides to have a left child with probability 1/2 and a right child with probability 1/2. What is the probability that the resulting tree is symmetric (i.e., its left subtree is a mirror image of its right subtree)?

title: Order Probabilities and Expectations for I.I.D. Variables
statement:
Let $X_1, X_2, \dots$ be a sequence of i.i.d. random variables from a continuous distribution. 
(a) Compute $P(X_1 < X_2)$. 
(b) Compute $P(X_{10} = \min\{X_9, X_{10}, X_{11}\})$. 
(c) Find the expected index $i > 1$ of the first variable $X_i$ such that $X_i < X_1$.

title: Effect of Duplicating Data on Regression Statistics
statement: You are given a dataset of $(x,y)$ pairs. A new dataset is created by duplicating every pair. If you run a simple linear regression, how do the following statistics change compared to the regression on the original dataset: (a) the estimated slope coefficient, (b) the R-squared value, and (c) the t-statistic for the slope?

title: Bayesian Inference with a Bag of Coins
statement: You have a bag with $n$ coins, where the $i$-th coin has a probability $p_i$ of landing heads. You randomly select one coin, flip it, and it comes up heads. What is the probability that the next flip of this same coin will also result in heads?

title: Coding: Reverse Polish to Infix Notation
statement: Write a program to convert an expression from Reverse Polish Notation (RPN) to standard infix notation. Ensure that the resulting expression does not have any unnecessary parentheses.

title: Coding: Optimal Task Scheduling
statement: You are given $n$ tasks and a set of dependencies representing the required order of execution for some pairs of tasks (e.g., task A must be completed before task B). Find an execution sequence that minimizes the completion time of task 1, and subject to that, minimizes the completion time of task 2, and so on, up to task $n$.

title: Coding: Largest Zero Submatrix
statement: Given a binary matrix (containing only 0s and 1s), find the area of the largest submatrix that contains only 0s.

title: Stochastic Processes and Sampling
statement:
This section covers a discussion on advanced topics.
(a) What are the key properties of a standard Brownian motion? What is its probability density function?
(b) For a Brownian bridge, what are its mean and variance?
(c) Can Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods be used to estimate parameters for a time series with discontinuities or jumps? How would you handle potential sampling biases, for example in graph sampling?

title: Linear Regression: R-squared Properties
statement: What is the definition of $R^2$? Is $R^2$ always non-negative in a linear regression model? What if the model is fitted without an intercept term?

title: Estimation with Constraints
